fb85594f2861ba90213b7f294cd24967283c8698: Maurach – Rofan is a little-known resort on a modest scale: 11 km of runs for an intimate skiing experience, far from the bustle of the big resorts. This is where you come for calm, authenticity and no queues at the lifts. Maurach – Rofan has kept the identity of an authentic mountain village, far from the concrete resorts of the 1970s. People come here for clean air, unspoiled landscapes and a friendly atmosphere that stands apart from the industrialisation of skiing in some large ski areas. Maurach – Rofan's moderate altitude, starting at 980 m with a summit at 1870 m, makes it sensitive to climate variations. January and February remain the most reliable months for good snow cover. Outside that window, checking snow reports before you leave is strongly advised. The 45€ day lift pass places Maurach – Rofan among the mid-range resorts on price: neither cheap nor exorbitant. The quality of the ski area and its facilities justifies the price for most skiers. In short: Maurach – Rofan doesn't rival the giants of skiing and doesn't pretend to. It's an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.

fbfe5cdcf2e980bf42a36c6576bce33a19ee053e: A resort on a human scale, Passo San Pellegrino prioritises the quality of its welcome and its closeness over impressive figures. Its 68 km of runs are ideal for a 3 to 4 day stay, especially for families or skiers who do not need to constantly change their playground. Passo San Pellegrino has managed to keep the identity of an authentic mountain village, far from the concrete resorts of the 1970s. People come here for the clean air, the unspoilt landscapes and a friendly atmosphere that stands apart from the industrialisation of skiing in some large ski areas. With a summit at 2,513 m and a village at 1,190 m, snow cover at Passo San Pellegrino is generally reliable from January to the end of March. A few exceptionally mild winters can cause strains early in the season, but conditions recover quickly after the first significant snowfalls. The budget for a stay at Passo San Pellegrino is clearly high: €71 for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants that are among the most expensive in the Alps. It is the price of excellence, but you should be aware of it before you set off. In short, Passo San Pellegrino keeps its promises. A resort in the Northern Alps that will suit most skier profiles without disappointing.
